result.text: The Brio kettle warranty lasts **47 months from the date it is delivered**. The passages refer to a kettle, not a water boiler.

Before first use:

1. Read the supplied installation instructions. If they are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home before installing.
2. Check the dryer and packaging for damage. If the casing, door, plug or electrical parts appear damaged, keep it disconnected and report the problem.
3. Choose a dry, ventilated indoor location, away from water, heat sources and open flames. Keep it at least **113 cm from a gas hob or open flame**. Follow the required clearances and keep ventilation openings unobstructed.
4. Set it on a firm, stable, level floor and adjust the feet so it stands securely without rocking. Don’t use improvised supports or enclose it unless the instructions allow.
5. Position it within **297 cm of a suitable earthed wall socket**. Keep the plug accessible and the lead unstretched, untrapped and out of walkways. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor; ask a qualified electrician if the socket is unsuitable.
6. Connect any vent hose or drainage fittings as the instructions specify, without twisting, crushing or trapping them.
7. Remove packaging from inside and around the drum, keep it away from children and pets, then wipe the empty drum with a soft, damp cloth.

If the cable is damaged or you’re unsure about the electrical supply, don’t connect the dryer—seek qualified help.

Orrin heat pumps warm rooms gradually, and they typically run at lower heating-water temperatures than boilers. As a result, the radiators may feel cooler even when the system is heating normally. Cold weather and defrost cycles can temporarily slow heating further.
The Fenwick cooker hood needs a 2.4 GHz home Wi-Fi network. It cannot connect to a network set to 5 GHz only.

Unplug the kettle and let it cool completely. Empty it, open the lid, and gently remove the filter from behind the spout—don’t force it if it’s stuck. Rinse it under warm running water and use a soft brush to loosen deposits. For stubborn limescale, soak the filter in warm water for 10 minutes, then brush gently and rinse thoroughly. Refit it securely before using the kettle.

Avoid abrasive cleaners and metal brushes, and never immerse the kettle body, base, or plug in water.

Before you leave, run a wash, then unload the dishwasher and let the interior cool. Clean the filter as described in the user manual and wipe the door seals with a soft, damp cloth. For an extended absence, switch off the electricity and close the water supply valve. Leave the door slightly open if it’s safe to do so. If the cottage could freeze, ask a qualified installer about draining the appliance. On your return, restore the supplies and check for leaks before running a wash.

The passages don’t specify a warranty period for a kitchen vent fan. They state that the Fenwick cooker hood is covered for 66 months from delivery, while the Brio kettle has a two-year warranty from purchase.

Leave a short, appliance-specific instruction sheet beside the machine. For a Keel washing machine, tell visitors to follow its supplied operating instructions, not to use it if it leaks, rocks, makes unusual noises, or shows a warning they cannot resolve, and to contact you or Halvard Home for help. If E-4020 appears, they should stop the programme, switch off and unplug the machine, and contact you rather than attempt installation work.

For an Ashby tumble dryer, tell visitors not to block its ventilation openings, use an extension lead or adaptor, or operate it if it appears damaged or unsafe. They should stop using it and contact you if they notice a problem.

Keep the instructions and any relevant safety or recall notice accessible. Don’t ask guests to move, install, or repair an appliance; arrange a competent professional when needed.

Stop the programme, switch off the dryer and unplug it. Let it cool, then clear the lint filter, empty and refit the water tank if your model has one, and check that clothing isn’t trapped in the door. Reconnect it and try the programme once. If the warning returns, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support; tell them which light is flashing and when it appears.

Stop cooking and switch the hob off using its controls. Remove anything covering the controls, and check that the control area is clean and dry. If it’s safe, you can try switching the hob off at the wall isolator for 60 seconds, then restoring power.

If the error returns, leave the hob off and contact Halvard Home support. Note the exact message and when it appears. Don’t open the hob or attempt internal repairs.

If you find ice inside your Tessa dishwasher, don’t start a programme. Switch it off and contact Halvard Home support for advice before using it again. Don’t use boiling water or sharp tools to remove the ice, as they could damage the dishwasher.

If you have a Halvard Home Lumen thermostat, use its heating schedule: set the time you want heating to begin (for example, set it to 19:00 for a one-hour delay from 18:00), choose your target temperature, and save. Make sure the schedule is enabled and set for the right day. Heating will only start if the room is cooler than the target temperature.
Keep the extractor running for 10 minutes after cooking to clear lingering steam and smells.

If your extractor hood’s screen is blank, check that its wall switch or fused spur is on. Try the light and fan controls to see whether the whole hood has lost power or just the display.

Switch the hood off at its electrical supply for 60 seconds, then turn it back on and try the controls again. Keep your hands dry around electrical switches. If the fan and light work but the screen stays blank, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which controls respond.

If nothing works, check whether other kitchen appliances have power. Don’t remove covers or touch internal wiring; arrange a qualified inspection if the problem continues.

Stop the dryer immediately and switch it off. Unplug it only if it is safe to do so; don’t run another cycle to test it.

If there’s smoke or flame, keep the door closed, leave the property and call 999. Don’t use water or try to move the dryer. If there’s no sign of fire, leave it unplugged until it has cooled completely, then you can clear fluff from the lint filter and check that the external vents are clear. Don’t use it again until a qualified appliance technician has checked it.
Yes. A factory reset clears saved Wi-Fi details, heating schedules, and personal settings. Note down any routines or preferences you want to restore, and have your Wi-Fi password ready.

To update your appliance’s built-in programming (firmware), the exact steps depend on the model:

- **Keel washing machine:** Finish the wash programme, empty the drum and leave the machine on and connected to Wi‑Fi. In the Halvard Home app, select the machine and go to **Settings > Firmware update**. Tap **Install** if an update is available.
- **Ashby tumble dryer:** Finish the drying programme, empty the drum, and leave the dryer on and connected to Wi‑Fi. On its display, open **Settings > Software update > Check for updates**, then select **Install** if available.
- **Tessa dishwasher:** Make sure no programme is running, empty the dishwasher, and leave it on and connected to Wi‑Fi. On the control panel, select **Firmware update > Check for updates**, then choose **Install** if available.
- **Vale fridge freezer:** Keep it connected to Wi‑Fi with steady power. On the control panel, go to **Settings > Software update > Check for updates** and follow the instructions.

For all models, keep the appliance powered on during installation and wait for its app or display to confirm the update is complete before using it.

To safely relocate your clothes dryer:

- Switch it off, unplug it, and let it cool completely if it has been running.
- Remove the laundry, clean the lint filter, empty the water tank if fitted, and disconnect any drain or vent hose.
- Secure the hoses and power cable so they cannot drag or catch.
- Plan a clear route, protect the floor without making it slippery, and keep children and pets away.
- Use two people and suitable handling equipment, such as an appliance trolley. Keep the dryer upright; never lift it by the door, control panel, cable, or fittings. Protect the cabinet and secure the dryer during transport.
- At the new location, set it on a firm, level floor, reconnect it according to its installation instructions, and check that it is secure and undamaged.

The safety policy also says to keep the dryer unplugged for **38 hours after moving it** before switching it on.
Hire a qualified heat pump installer to disconnect, move and recommission your Orrin heat pump. Don’t move it while it’s still connected to wiring or pipework.

Send the service team:

- Your cooktop’s full model name, from the purchase paperwork or appliance label.
- A clear photo of the part you want to replace, if you still have it. If it’s missing, describe what it does.
- A short description of the part you need.

Ask them to confirm it’s compatible with your exact model, and check the part price, delivery charge and estimated delivery time before ordering.

Make sure your Mira vacuum is online in the Halvard Home app and that you can start a clean from there. In your voice assistant’s app, add a smart-home service, search for **Halvard Home**, and sign in with the same account you used to set up Mira. Allow access, then ask the assistant to discover devices.

Give the vacuum a simple name, such as “Mira,” and try saying, “Start Mira.” If it doesn’t appear, check its internet connection, unlink Halvard Home in the assistant app, and link it again.

If your Orrin heat pump isn’t showing up in the Halvard Home app:

1. Make sure the heat pump is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi.
2. Move your phone closer to the heat pump.
3. Allow the app Bluetooth and local network access in your phone’s settings.
4. Turn your phone’s Wi‑Fi off for 10 seconds, then back on.
5. Close and reopen the app, then try adding the heat pump again. Check for an app update if needed.

If it still doesn’t appear, contact Halvard Home support with your phone model and what happens when you try to connect.

For a safe relocation:

- Switch off the cooktop and let the surface cool. Have a qualified electrician isolate and disconnect its fixed wiring—don’t rely on a dark display or pull on the cable.
- Clear the route, protect the glass from knocks, and arrange suitable help or lifting equipment. Keep children and pets away.
- Lift only by the handling points specified in the installation instructions, not by the cable, controls or glass edges. Do not force it past obstructions.
- Protect it in suitable packaging and secure it against sliding or impact. Do not put anything on top or let the cable be crushed.
- **Do not tilt the Corra induction hob more than 48 degrees while carrying it.**
- After moving it, wait **31 hours** before switching it on. This does not replace inspection or professional reconnection.
- Have a qualified installer check the new location, stability, ventilation, cable routing and electrical safety. Leave it disconnected and contact Halvard Home if it was dropped, struck, exposed to water, damaged, or otherwise seems unsafe.

If you’re leaving food inside, keep the refrigerator running, set it to 4°C, and make sure the door closes properly. Remove anything that will expire before you return.

If you’re emptying it for the months away, switch it off and unplug it before cleaning. Remove all food, let any ice thaw, wipe the interior with warm water and mild detergent, and dry it thoroughly. Leave the doors ajar to help prevent smells and mould. When you return, let the appliance reach its set temperature before adding chilled food.

To prepare your Keel washer for a move:

1. Switch it off at the socket and unplug it. Turn off the water supply, disconnect the inlet hose, and drain any remaining water, using a towel and shallow tray to catch spills.
2. Empty the drum and leave it dry.
3. Refit the original transport bolts according to the user manual. They secure the drum during transport. If they’re missing, contact Halvard Home before moving the washer.
4. Secure the hoses and cable without stretching them. Keep the washer upright, use two people, and don’t carry or pull it by its door, controls, hoses or cable.
5. At the new home, remove the transport bolts before using the washer. Follow the installation instructions; the safety policy also says to leave it upright and disconnected for 44 hours after moving before switching it on.

Warm, moist cooking air can condense into droplets when it meets the cold hood or extraction duct. This is more noticeable in chilly weather, especially if the duct runs through an unheated space. Start the hood when you begin cooking, leave it on for 10 minutes afterwards, and keep the kitchen ventilated.

Stop the programme and note the exact error message. Switch the washer off and unplug it for five minutes, then check that the door is fully closed and no clothing is caught in the seal. Don’t force the door open if water remains inside, and only handle the plug with dry hands. If the message returns, stop using the washer and contact Halvard Home support with the message and when it appeared.

Provide the full model details from the cooker hood’s rating label and the name or a short description of the accessory you need. If you still have the old part, include a clear photo; if you’re unsure what it’s called, explain what you want to replace. Ask support to confirm it fits your exact model, along with availability, the total cost including delivery and the expected delivery time.

Use the Mira robot vacuum’s child lock: while the vacuum is switched on and stationary, press and hold the power button for 3 seconds. A sound confirms the lock is active.

The lock disables the vacuum’s physical buttons, but scheduled cleaning and controls in the Halvard Home app still work, so it may start automatically. Keep your toddler away while it’s moving.

Warm, moist air may be getting into the fridge, often because the doors are opened frequently, food is uncovered, or something prevents a door from sealing properly. Set the fridge to 4°C, make sure both doors close fully, clean and dry the door seals, cover food, and keep the air vents clear. Wipe away condensation with a clean cloth.

If thick ice builds up, unplug the appliance and move food to suitable cold storage before defrosting. Don’t use sharp tools or a hairdryer. Contact Halvard Home support if the ice or dampness keeps returning.

Check the power supply first: make sure the plug is fully inserted and the wall socket is switched on. You can test the socket with a lamp you know works. If the socket works, unplug the dryer briefly, reconnect it, close the door firmly and try switching it on again.

If you mean the Mira robot vacuum, place it on its plugged-in charging dock. Hold the **Power** and **Home** buttons together for 10 seconds, then release them when you hear the reset announcement. Leave it on the dock while it restarts.

The reset removes saved Wi-Fi details, maps and cleaning schedules. After restarting, add the vacuum again in the Halvard Home app and reconnect it to Wi-Fi.

Recycle heating equipment separately from household rubbish. Use a recycling service or centre that accepts the specific appliance, and check its booking and collection arrangements first.

For a heat pump, have a qualified installer disconnect it and safely recover the refrigerant; don’t dismantle it yourself. For an installed thermostat, ask a qualified electrician or heating engineer to disconnect it safely. If the thermostat still works, reset it and remove it from your smart home account before recycling. Remove and recycle batteries separately only if they’re designed to be user-removable.
First, check that the extractor’s wall switch or fused connection switch is on. If it has a plug, make sure it’s fully inserted, but only if you can reach it safely.

Switch off the robot vacuum and remove it from its charging dock. Check the lid edges, hinges and catch for dust, hair or small objects, and wipe accessible areas with a dry, soft cloth. Make sure the dust bin is seated correctly and nothing sticks up above it, then lower the lid gently—don’t force it shut. If it still won’t stay down, or a hinge or catch looks damaged, stop using the vacuum and contact Halvard Home support.

If it’s a Brio electric kettle, switch it off and unplug it, let it cool completely, and empty it. Use a descaler labelled as suitable for kettles, following its instructions; don’t exceed the kettle’s maximum fill mark or mix cleaning products.

When treatment is finished, empty and rinse the kettle thoroughly. Fill it to the maximum mark, boil the water and discard it; repeat once before making drinks. Keep the kettle’s base, plug and exterior dry, and never immerse the kettle in water.

Switch the tea maker off and unplug it, then let it cool completely. If the plug or socket is wet, don’t touch it—turn off the electricity at the consumer unit first. Lift the kettle off its base and dry the outside. Check whether water has run down from the spout or lid, and keep the water below the MAX mark. If water is escaping from the bottom or the leak continues, stop using it and contact Halvard Home support. Don’t immerse the electrical base or try to repair it yourself.

Try these energy-saving steps while keeping your home comfortable:

- **Set heating thoughtfully:** Start around 19°C and adjust to suit everyone’s needs. Lowering your usual setting by 1°C can reduce energy use, as long as the home remains warm enough.
- **Use a schedule:** Match heating times to your routine. For heat pumps, try a small overnight temperature reduction rather than turning the heating off; for other systems, set lower temperatures when you’re out or asleep.
- **Avoid unnecessary boosts:** Turning the target temperature up sharply usually won’t warm a room faster. After using a temporary override, return to your schedule.
- **Keep your thermostat clear:** Furniture and curtains can interfere with its temperature readings.
- **Use appliances efficiently:** Set your fridge to 4°C and freezer to −18°C, avoid colder settings than needed, and keep doors closed. With a kettle, heat only the amount you need and switch off keep-warm when you don’t need it.
- **Keep equipment in good shape:** Descale the kettle regularly, and ask your installer to check heat-pump settings if rooms are consistently too warm or too cold.

Some people, including older adults or those with health conditions, may need a warmer home.

For a Vale fridge freezer, first check that food, bottles or packaging aren’t blocking the door. Push drawers fully in and make sure shelves are seated correctly. Clean the rubber seal and the surface it meets with warm water and a soft cloth, then dry both. Check for freezer ice blocking the door, but don’t chip it with a sharp tool or force the door shut.

If the door still hangs unevenly or the seal is split, contact Halvard Home support and keep the door closed as much as possible.

For a Tessa dishwasher, connect it to your home Wi‑Fi, make sure no wash programme is running, empty it and leave it switched on. On the control panel, go to **Settings > Firmware update > Check for updates**. If an update is available, select **Install** and follow the display instructions. Keep the power and Wi‑Fi connected until the display confirms the update is complete.

Contact Halvard Home customer support with your washer’s model details and a description of the part. Send a clear photo of the identification label, and photograph the original part too if you still have it. Explain that you want an extra item rather than a replacement, and ask support to confirm compatibility, availability, the total price including delivery, and the expected delivery time before ordering.

Pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop. If the door unlocks, spread heavy items evenly around the drum, then restart the programme—never force the door open. Check that the machine is firmly on a hard, level floor, with all four feet touching and no rocking. If it was newly installed, check the installation guide to ensure the transit bolts were removed. If strong vibration continues, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support.

Stop the cycle and turn off the water supply tap. Switch off and unplug the machine only if the plug and surrounding area are dry—never touch a wet plug or socket. When safe, wipe up the water and check visible inlet-hose connections, whether the drain hose has slipped out, and whether water is running from the detergent drawer (excess detergent can cause foaming and leaks).

Don’t run another cycle while the cause is unexplained. If the hoses seem secure or water is coming from beneath the casing, contact Halvard Home support.

Make sure the washing machine is switched on and your phone is nearby. Connect your phone to a **2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network** (5 GHz won’t work for setup), turn on Bluetooth, and allow the app to access nearby devices. Close and reopen the app, then try adding the machine again and follow the pairing instructions.

If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and router and try again once Wi-Fi is available. If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support with your phone model and where setup stops.

Stop cleaning and switch off the vacuum. If the dock or plug is wet, switch off the mains socket before handling it.

Remove and empty the water tank over a sink. Check that the filler cap is fully closed and inspect the tank and outlet for cracks. Wipe the tank and vacuum underside dry; don’t rinse the vacuum body or return it to the dock while wet.

If the tank is cracked or it leaks again after you refit it securely, stop using the mopping function and contact Halvard Home support.

Make sure the heat pump is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Then try these steps in order:

1. Move your phone closer to the heat pump.
2. Allow the app any requested Bluetooth or local network access in your phone’s settings.
3. Turn Wi‑Fi off for 10 seconds, then turn it back on.
4. Close the app completely, reopen it, and try adding the device again.
5. Check your app store for an app update.

If the heat pump still doesn’t appear, contact Halvard Home support and tell them your phone model and what happens when you try to connect.

Start with the controller’s power supply: tap the display in case it’s asleep, and check that any clearly labelled power switch is on. If it uses replaceable batteries, fit fresh ones, matching the + and − markings. Don’t remove the cover or touch wiring. If it remains dark, contact Halvard Home support; if you notice a burning smell, unusual heat, or damaged wiring, stop using it and contact a qualified electrician.
Yes. A gentle rumbling or hissing sound while the Brio kettle heats is usually normal. A click when it switches off is expected too.
No. The Brio kettle has no timer or delay-start setting; you must switch it on manually when you’re ready to boil water.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let it cool. Clean and refit the fluff filter, empty and securely replace the water tank if your model has one, and check that no clothing is caught in the door. Then reconnect the dryer and try the programme again. If the light keeps flashing, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support, explaining which light flashes and when.

Yes. Water beneath the outdoor unit during or shortly after defrosting is usually normal: ice on the outdoor coil melts and drains away. Monitor it to see whether it stops. If water runs continuously, appears to come from a pipe joint, or you can’t safely identify the source, contact Halvard Home support or a qualified heat pump engineer.

A rattling, thumping or scraping noise may be caused by loose objects in the drum, metal zips or buttons, an uneven load, or the dryer touching nearby furniture.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let the drum cool before checking for loose items. Redistribute bulky laundry evenly, then make sure the dryer stands firmly on a level floor and isn’t touching a wall or cupboard. Don’t reach underneath or remove any panels.

If the noise continues or you hear loud grinding, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support.

Switch off and unplug the machine, and let any hot water cool completely. Open the lower front filter flap with towels and a shallow tray underneath. Slowly turn the filter anticlockwise to drain trapped water, then remove it, clear away lint and other debris, and rinse it.
